note: Decoy secrets `topgent honeytoken plant <dir>` writes, and the card a read of one raises. Each decoy's path is relative to the folder it is planted in and must match the sensitive-file catalogue as its `class`, so the collector records the read by name without opening anything. Placeholders in `content` are filled with fresh random values at planting: {{key_id}} an AWS-shaped access key id, {{secret}} 40 base64 characters, {{token}} a `tgh_`-prefixed token, {{blob}} a long base64 block. The values are never stored: the manifest keeps paths, classes, sizes and times.

decoys.content:
-- dump of users
INSERT INTO users (email, api_token) VALUES ('ops@example.com', '{{token}}');

card.name: Honeytoken Accessed
why: Decoy secret planted with `topgent honeytoken plant`. No task needs it; any read is a finding.
Opening a decoy credential indicates a search for credentials.
actions: Stop the program and check what else it read and where it connected.
Treat any real secret in the same places as disclosed: rotate the keys and tokens it could reach.
limits: Any program that opens the file raises this, including grep, indexers and backup tools. The card names the program.
The read is recorded by file name. Contents are not read.
The planted-path list is in the user's state folder. An agent running as the user can edit it and remove an alarm.
